record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.context_brief: Limits of Lyapunov methods for iISS
record.original_question: Determine whether the existence of integral-input-to-state-stable infinite-dimensional systems that are not input-to-state stable would reveal genuine limitations of Lyapunov methods for systems with unbounded input operators, and if so, characterize how severe those limitations are. The issue is tied to the fact that ISS Lyapunov functions are automatically iISS Lyapunov functions.

evidence.quote: • ISS Lyapunov functions are by definition iISS Lyapunov functions. Thus the existence of iISS systems which are not ISS would suggest, that there are some limitations of the Lyapunov method at least for systems with unbounded input operators. Whether such limitations exist at all and how significant they are is a completely open question right now.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider control systems of the form
  x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),  x(0) = x_0,
on a Banach space X, where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup and B: U → X_{-1} is a (possibly unbounded) admissible input operator from a Banach space U of input values; admissible inputs u belong to L^∞(0,∞;U). Let β denote the class of KL-functions and let K, K_∞, P denote the standard comparison-function classes.

The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that, for every initial state x_0 ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})  for all t ≥ 0.

It is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL, θ ∈ K_∞ and μ ∈ K such that
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + θ( ∫_0^t μ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds )  for all t ≥ 0.

A continuous functional V: X → [0,∞) is called an ISS-Lyapunov function if it satisfies coercive bounds ψ_1(‖x‖) ≤ V(x) ≤ ψ_2(‖x‖) with ψ_1, ψ_2 ∈ K_∞, and an appropriate dissipation inequality of ISS type along trajectories; an iISS-Lyapunov function satisfies analogous bounds with an iISS dissipation inequality. Every ISS-Lyapunov function is automatically an iISS-Lyapunov function.

Question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional control system of the above form, with an unbounded input operator B, that is integral input-to-state stable but not input-to-state stable? If such a system exists, quantify in what precise sense its existence reveals limitations of the Lyapunov-function approach to verifying ISS for systems with unbounded input operators, and characterize how severe these limitations are (e.g., whether iISS-Lyapunov functions can fail to detect the absence of ISS, and to what extent the Lyapunov method remains a complete tool for ISS in this setting).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2024–2025) on ISS/iISS for infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators continues to develop coercive and noncoercive ISS-Lyapunov methods, generalized ISS-Lyapunov functionals, and iISS-Lyapunov constructions for parabolic/hyperbolic PDEs with boundary disturbances. None of the surveyed works exhibits an iISS but not ISS infinite-dimensional system with unbounded B, nor rules it out; the question of whether such systems exist (and what limitations of the Lyapunov method this would entail) is still treated as an open problem in current surveys and tutorials.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems: Recent Results and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing the existence of iISS-but-not-ISS systems with unbounded input operators, and the resulting limitations of the Lyapunov method, as a completely open question.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as an open question in the survey on ISS of infinite-dimensional systems.

status_evidence.title: A Unified Lyapunov Method for ISS of PDEs (tutorial)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses generalized/noncoercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for PDEs with boundary disturbances modeled by unbounded input operators, but does not produce or exclude iISS-but-not-ISS examples.
status_evidence.claim: Recent tutorials continue developing Lyapunov methods without resolving the iISS-vs-ISS gap for unbounded B.

status_evidence.title: Lyapunov methods for input-to-state stability of time-varying evolution equations
status_evidence.snippet: Provides Lyapunov-based sufficient conditions for LISS and iISS of time-varying evolution equations; the iISS-vs-ISS gap question for unbounded inputs is not settled.
status_evidence.claim: Current Lyapunov-method developments leave the iISS-not-ISS question for unbounded input operators unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper constructing coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular linear systems with unbounded input operators; works toward but does not close the gap.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art constructions advance ISS-Lyapunov theory for unbounded B but do not resolve the open question.
